message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001784","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All candidates are direct label matches for abdominal aortic aneurysm, so selection hinges on PRS-comparable performance evidence and study/method signals. Per the performance-metrics guidance, PRS-only (or covariates-regressed-out) R² is the most comparable indicator; PGS001784 reports a PRS-comparable Nagelkerke R² (covariates regressed out) of 0.014661 in a large European validation (n=350,767) using a modern genome-wide Bayesian method (PRS-CS-auto). Competing models either lack PRS-comparable metrics (PGS002054 only partial-r; PGS003429/PGS003972/PGS003973 mainly full-model AUROC/C-index with unknown/basic covariates) or are a very small-variant P+T score with only an OR per SD (PGS000753). The very high full-model AUROC/C-index values (e.g., 0.868/0.882) are likely covariate-influenced and are not treated as PRS-only evidence. Heritability lookup for closely related EUR endpoints (UKBB ‘aortic aneurysm and dissection’) shows low observed h2 but nonzero liability-scale h2 (~0.02 to ~0.106), making a PRS-only R² around ~0.015 plausible and interpretable rather than obviously inflated. Therefore PGS001784 is the best-supported, most comparable choice, with moderate confidence due to endpoint/metric heterogeneity across the remaining candidates."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002738","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Using the PRS Model Evaluator framework (read_skill_section: skill_overview), I prioritized endpoint fidelity plus the most interpretable/robust performance evidence available across candidates. For the target trait alcohol dependence, the most direct labels are the two “Alcohol use disorder / alcohol dependence” models (PGS002738, PGS002739), whereas PGS000201/PGS000202 are for “Problematic alcohol use” with a DSM-5 criteria-count phenotype (adjacent but less directly case/control AUD).

Between the direct-endpoint options, PGS002738 is the best match because it is validated in Europeans (matching the other EUR-evaluated candidates) with a reasonably large validation sample (n=7,900) and provides a clear discrimination-style metric (OR top 10% vs rest = 1.96, 95% CI 1.54–2.51). PGS002739 is evaluated only in African American/Afro-Caribbean samples, making it less suitable as a general pick from this list when the other direct model has EUR evaluation.

The older EUR “problematic alcohol use” scores (PGS000201/PGS000202) report only small incremental ΔR² (0.0119 and 0.0046) and are tied to a specific covariate set, making cross-record comparison harder than the direct AUD OR metric.

Heritability sanity-check (get_heritability_records: alcohol dependence) shows modest SNP h2 in EUR (e.g., h2_liability ~0.18 for an alcohol dependency discovery record), consistent with expecting only modest standalone PRS performance; this supports treating the available OR/ΔR² signals as incremental rather than expecting very high predictive accuracy from any candidate."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004913","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity: all three candidates map to the target EFO (alcoholic liver cirrhosis), but PGS004913 is explicitly built for “Alcohol-associated liver cirrhosis” in heavy drinkers, matching the intended clinical construct without being a broad proxy.

Performance evidence (per performance_metrics guidance): none of the candidates report PRS-only AUROC/R²; two report only full-model discrimination (PGS000704 C-index 0.711 with basic covariates; PGS001777 AUROC 0.671 with unknown covariates). PGS004913 instead reports an R²=0.029 and OR(top vs bottom decile)=4.4, which—while not explicitly labeled PRS-only—provides more direct PRS contribution evidence than full-model AUROC/C-index alone, and uses a basic covariate set (age/sex/PCs).

Study design/scale tradeoff: PGS000704 has very large UKB training and many variants, but it is a high-throughput framework score with only full-model time-to-event C-index reported, making standalone PRS strength harder to infer. PGS001777 is a 3-variant score with small validation (n=1,390) and unknown covariates, increasing uncertainty. PGS004913 is disease-focused and recent, with a modest but interpretable variance explained and effect size in a relevant heavy-drinker context.

Heritability sanity check: local EUR h2 records for related liver disease/cirrhosis endpoints show low observed-scale h2 (~0.001–0.008; e.g., ICD10 K70 alcoholic liver disease h2≈0.0013; K74 fibrosis/cirrhosis h2≈0.0083). Against this backdrop, an R² of 0.029 is plausible as a reported variance-explained metric in a specific high-risk (heavy drinker) sample rather than a general-population observed-scale ceiling, but it also argues for only moderate confidence overall.

Overall, PGS004913 offers the best combination of direct endpoint targeting and the most PRS-informative reported performance among the fixed candidates, with reasonably clean covariate adjustment."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001262","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All candidates are direct EFO matches to angina pectoris, but the most comparable cross-model performance evidence is PRS-only (no-covariate) metrics (per performance_metrics guidance). Among models that report PRS-only metrics, PGS001262 has the strongest PRS-only discrimination/variance (PGS AUROC(no covariates)=0.58683; PGS R2(no covariates)=0.01304) and the largest incremental AUROC (0.0098) versus the other snpnet angina endpoints (PGS001260/PGS001261). Several newer ICD10/PheCode-based scores (e.g., PGS004457/PGS004527/PGS00504x/PGS00505x) lack PRS-only AUC/R2 and mostly report full-model C-index or per-SD ORs, making them less comparable for selecting a standalone PGS from this fixed list. Heritability records for angina pectoris (UKB ICD10 I20) show low observed-scale h2 (~0.01–0.016; liability-scale ~0.09–0.19), consistent with the modest PRS-only R2 values seen here and not suggesting any metric misuse; thus PGS001262’s slightly higher PRS-only R2 is a meaningful (if small) edge. Confidence is moderate because all top candidates are UKB-derived and differences in PRS-only metrics are small."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001267","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All candidates are for ankylosing spondylitis, but PGS001267 and PGS001268 differ by endpoint framing: PGS001267 matches the target trait directly, whereas PGS001268 is a time-to-event variant (less directly comparable for a generic disease-risk PGS). Per the performance-metrics guidance (read_skill_section: performance_metrics), PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUC/R²) should be prioritized over full-model AUROC; PGS001267 reports PGS-only AUROC=0.7265 and PGS-only R²=0.0988 in European validation with basic covariates, making it directly comparable and well-supported. The UKB portability-study scores (PGS001876/PGS002089) lack AUC/R² and only provide partial-r, and the Taiwan EAS scores report only full-model AUROC with unknown covariates and small validation N, so they are less reliable for general selection. Heritability lookup for ankylosing spondylitis (get_heritability_records) shows EUR liability-scale h2 estimates roughly ~0.14–0.40 depending on phenotype definition, which makes the reported PRS-only R² (~0.10) plausible (not exceeding a reasonable genetic-variance ceiling) and supports interpreting PGS001267’s PRS-only metrics as credible."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS005252","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Target trait is aortic stenosis; among candidates, only PGS005252/PGS005254 are directly labeled aortic stenosis (PGS005255/PGS005256 are aortic valve function measurements; others are hypertrophic cardiomyopathy). PGS005252 has the strongest record-visible evaluation signal: large EUR evaluation sample (n=446,895), modern genome-wide method (LDPred2; 1,119,377 variants), and a reported time-to-event discrimination metric (C-index 0.87) plus HR=1.92. PGS005254 reports only an HR (1.64) with no AUC/C-index/R², making it harder to judge predictive quality from the metadata. PGS005252’s reported performance is a full model adjusted for multiple clinical covariates (packaging risk per the evaluator framework), so the C-index likely reflects combined clinical+PGS prediction rather than PRS-only; nonetheless, within this fixed list it remains the best-supported direct-endpoint model. Heritability lookup for 'aortic stenosis' returned no close matches (only unrelated 'stenosis' traits with match_score 0), so h2 cannot be used to calibrate expected R²/AUC here; decision is therefore driven primarily by endpoint fidelity and the presence/strength of reported validation performance."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001135","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity: the target trait is generic “arthritis”, and PGS001135 is the only candidate whose trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported directly match this umbrella endpoint (phenotyping_reported: “Arthritis (nos)”), whereas most other candidates are specific arthritis subtypes (e.g., rheumatoid arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, osteoarthritis, gout, juvenile idiopathic arthritis) and therefore are not direct matches for a generic arthritis target (per trait-label endpoint-fidelity guidance from read_skill_section('trait_labels')). Performance interpretation: PGS001135 reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates 0.539; PGS R2 no covariates 0.00291) plus incremental AUROC (0.00314), which are more comparable indicators of PRS contribution than full-model AUROC alone (per read_skill_section('performance_metrics')). Heritability sanity-check: local EUR h2 records for arthritis-adjacent endpoints include “Non-cancer illness code, self-reported: arthritis (nos)” with low observed-scale h2 (~0.0006–0.0045 across UKB-LDSC records) and “Other arthritis” with h2 ~0.002–0.007, suggesting limited common-variant signal for broad/heterogeneous arthritis definitions; PGS001135’s modest PRS-only R2 is directionally consistent with these ceilings, while higher full-model AUCs in other candidates are likely driven by covariates and/or different, narrower phenotypes rather than a better generic-arthritis PRS."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001344","confidence":"High","rationale":"Using the PRS-evaluation framework (prs_model_evaluator skill_overview + performance_metrics): prioritize endpoint fidelity, PRS-comparable metrics (PGS-only AUROC/R2 when available), and clean/basic covariate adjustment over full-model AUROC that may be covariate-driven.

Among the direct asthma candidates, the UKB snpnet models provide explicit PRS-only metrics. PGS001344 ("Asthma diagnosed by doctor") has the strongest PRS-only performance in the list (PGS-only AUROC 0.64568; PGS-only R2 0.05973) and correspondingly strong full-model AUROC 0.66621 with only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). It also has large training (n=216,121) and substantial validation (n=19,857; EUR).

Heritability sanity-check (get_heritability_records for asthma): EUR h2 estimates for asthma/doctor-diagnosed asthma are on the order of ~0.05–0.07 in UKB-LDSC records (with some higher estimates in other sources/definitions). A PRS-only R2 ~0.06 is plausible relative to these ceilings and does not look like an obvious reporting artifact.

Other candidates either lack PRS-only metrics (many report only full-model AUROC or incremental R2), have much smaller validation/training, or show weaker PRS-only performance (e.g., other snpnet asthma definitions around PGS-only R2 ~0.037). Therefore PGS001344 is the best-supported, directly aligned, high-quality choice from the fixed list."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002755","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity: target is atopic eczema. PGS002755 is directly aligned (trait_reported: Atopic dermatitis; trait_efo: atopic eczema) with appropriate general-population incident AD phenotyping, whereas PGS003459/PGS003486/PGS004903 are primarily about paradoxical eczema in biologic-treated psoriasis (mismatched endpoint context) and PGS001773 is restricted to moderate-to-severe AD (narrower severity-defined endpoint). Performance evidence: no candidate reports PRS-only AUC/R2; per the performance_metrics guidance, full-model AUROC/R2 (e.g., PGS001773 AUROC 0.93 with multiple demographic/ethnicity covariates) is not reliable for cross-model PRS ranking. In this setting, structural signals (method and genome-wide coverage) and effect-size magnitude are more informative; PGS002755 uses PRS-CS with ~1.09M variants and is evaluated in a large EUR sample (n=337,910) with a modest but non-trivial HR high-vs-low of 1.249, making it the most generalizable direct-match option in the list. Heritability sanity-check: local EUR h2 for eczema is modest (h2~0.071 observed; ~0.129 liability), consistent with expecting only moderate standalone PRS discrimination; this supports preferring a modern genome-wide method (PGS002755) over small-variant-set scores or covariate-inflated full-model metrics."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001340","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity: direct match to the target trait (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all atrial fibrillation), avoiding broader composites except closely related flutter variants. Performance evidence: among candidates, PGS001340 reports explicit PRS-comparable metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates ≈0.613; PGS R2 no covariates ≈0.0233) plus incremental AUROC (~0.020) and full-model AUROC (~0.776) with basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs). Per the performance_metrics guidance, PRS-only metrics are the most reliable cross-model discriminator; many other candidates report only full-model AUROC/C-index (often covariate-inflated) or only effect sizes without PRS-only discrimination. Study/implementation signals: large UKB development sample (n≈269,704) and sparse snpnet model (2,955 variants) with multi-ancestry evaluation reported, supporting robustness. Heritability sanity check: local EUR h2 records for atrial fibrillation are modest (observed h2 ~0.02–0.03; liability h2 ~0.055–0.064 in GWAS Atlas records), making a PRS-only R2 around 0.023 plausible and not obviously inconsistent, while very high full-model C-index values in some candidates are likely driven by clinical covariates/risk calculators rather than PRS alone."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001263","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity: PGS001263 is the only candidate with phenotyping_reported and trait_reported exactly matching the target (atrial flutter), whereas PGS001339/PGS001841/PGS002050 are broader atrial fibrillation+flutter composites (trait label guidance: phenotyping_reported is primary for endpoint fidelity; combined endpoints are acceptable but a clean direct endpoint has an advantage when performance is competitive). Comparable performance: PGS001263 reports explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS AUROC no covariates 0.617; PGS R2 no covariates 0.025), which are the most comparable indicators for PRS quality; its PRS-only AUROC/R2 are slightly higher than the closely related snpnet composite PGS001339 (0.613; 0.024). The other two candidates (PGS001841/PGS002050) lack PRS-only AUROC/R2 and only provide partial-r, making them harder to compare directly on discrimination. Covariates/packaging: PGS001263 uses only basic covariates (age, sex, array, PCs) and provides PRS-only metrics, reducing concern that full-model AUROC (~0.78) is driving the apparent performance (performance-metrics guidance). Heritability sanity check: local EUR h2 records for ICD10 I48 atrial fibrillation and flutter show low observed-scale h2 (~0.015–0.021; liability ~0.145–0.204), consistent with a modest PRS-only R2 (~0.025) and supporting that the reported PRS-only signal is plausible rather than obviously inflated."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000327","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Using the PRS evaluation framework (read_skill_section: skill_overview), the strongest differentiators here are endpoint fidelity and the cleanliness/comparability of the reported performance. PGS000327 is directly aligned across trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported (all autism spectrum disorder) and is based on a large ASD GWAS training set (n=28,592) with EUR-only train/eval matching; it reports a variance explained metric (full_model R²=0.0245) and an OR=1.33 with tight CI, suggesting a non-trivial polygenic signal for the intended endpoint. In contrast, PGS002790 has weaker endpoint fidelity (phenotyping_reported is ‘Psychiatric behavior (withdrawn)’ despite ASD labels), lacks a clear training sample size (samples_training N/A), and shows lower reported partial R² (~0.0055), making it a less direct and less compelling ASD score from the visible metadata.\n\nTrait heritability context (get_heritability_records: autism spectrum disorder) shows EUR h2 estimates around ~0.19–0.29 for ASD in GWAS Atlas records, indicating meaningful common-variant heritability; the ~2.45% variance explained reported for PGS000327 is plausible in that context and supports selecting it over the lower-performing/less-fidelitous alternative."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000454","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo (basal cell carcinoma) and are evaluated in EUR, but none report PRS-only AUROC/R2; most reported AUROCs/R2 are full-model with basic covariates (age/sex/PCs/batch), so we prioritize the strongest available PRS signal proxies (effect size per SD and pseudo-R²) per the performance-metrics guidance. Within the PRSweb/Cancer PRSweb family (same endpoint/covariates/validation N≈11,322), PGS000454 (P+T, 27 variants) has the top (or tied-top) full-model AUROC (0.632) and the highest Nagelkerke pseudo-R² (0.0489) among the MGI-evaluated models, with strong per-SD OR (1.661) and strong top-1% vs rest OR (3.79). Competing models with similar AUROC (e.g., PGS000452) are essentially tied but slightly lower pseudo-R² and/or top-1% OR. Models with larger variant counts (e.g., PRS-CS) show weaker performance here, and newer 2023/2025 scores lack comparable discrimination metrics in this candidate list. As a sanity check, local EUR heritability records for self-reported basal cell carcinoma show low observed-scale h2 (~0.01) but substantially higher liability-scale h2 (~0.14–0.21), consistent with modest-to-moderate PRS performance and not contradicting the selected model’s modest full-model AUROC and pseudo-R²."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS000924","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Using the PRS-model-evaluator framework (skill_overview), I prioritized endpoint fidelity plus availability of comparable PRS-only performance. PGS000924 targets a closely aligned endpoint (“Disorders of porphyrin and bilirubin metabolism” with EFO including bilirubin metabolism disease) and reports both PRS-only and full-model metrics in Europeans (PGS-only AUROC=0.88697; full-model AUROC=0.90591; PGS-only R²=0.21843), enabling cleaner comparison and reducing ambiguity about covariate-driven performance. The two alternatives (PGS001824, PGS002032) match the EFO label directly (“Disorders of bilirubin excretion”) but only report partial correlation (partial-r=0.0716) without AUROC/R², making them harder to evaluate on a comparable predictive-performance axis from the metadata alone; they are also essentially tied on the reported metric. As an advisory sanity-check, local EUR heritability records for bilirubin-related traits show modest h2 (e.g., ~0.089 with large SE), which is consistent with expecting limited-to-moderate variance explained and makes the presence of explicit PRS-only metrics in PGS000924 particularly valuable for interpretation. Overall, PGS000924 is the best-supported, directly relevant candidate in this fixed list, though confidence is moderated by the phenotype not being an exact match to “bilirubin excretion” and by the unusually small variant count (5) suggesting a sparse model that may be less robust across settings."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS002786","confidence":"Low","rationale":"Trait match: PGS002786 is the only candidate whose trait_reported/trait_efo directly matches the target (“Bipolar disorder”). Per the trait-label guidance, endpoint fidelity is driven primarily by phenotyping_reported; here, all three candidates have phenotyping_reported fields that appear unrelated to a direct bipolar disorder diagnosis (cognitive/behavioral measures), which is a warning signal for deployment to bipolar disorder risk.

Among the fixed candidates, I still select PGS002786 because it has the closest label alignment to the target compared with the Bipolar I (PGS002787) and Bipolar II (PGS002788) subtype scores.

Heritability sanity-check: local EUR h2 records for bipolar disorder show substantial SNP-heritability on the liability scale (e.g., ~0.17–0.27 in GWAS Atlas records), so the very low reported partial R² here is plausible given phenotype mismatch/packaging and does not indicate a high-performing clinical BD PRS in this candidate set."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS004153","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Target trait is breast carcinoma; several candidates directly match this endpoint (trait_efo=\"breast carcinoma\"). Following the PRS model evaluator guidance (skill_overview + performance_metrics), I prioritize (i) endpoint fidelity, (ii) PRS-comparable performance evidence when available, and (iii) avoiding covariate-packaged full-model metrics as the main ranking axis. Among direct-endpoint candidates, PGS004153 (UKBB-EUR.MultiPRS.CV) reports strong PRS-only-style evidence with covariates listed as 0 (minimizing covariate leakage concerns) and has the best full-model AUROC in the high-performing 2023 UKB-evaluated cluster (AUROC≈0.6625; R²≈0.0764) with a large European evaluation sample (n=48,968). Competing high-AUROC models like PGS000007 (AUROC 0.78) and PGS001336 (full-model AUROC 0.81) are heavily covariate-inflated (age/sex etc.) and/or show modest PGS-only AUROC (~0.596) and small incremental AUROC, making them less comparable as standalone PGS choices per the performance_metrics section. Heritability lookup for \"breast carcinoma\" returned mostly weak/poorly matched ICD10 carcinoma-in-situ records (low match_score), so h2 provides limited constraint here; nonetheless, the selected model’s reported R² (~0.076) is not obviously implausible relative to typical complex-disease ceilings, and the decision is driven primarily by the cleaner (covariates=0) performance reporting and strong direct-endpoint validation evidence."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001301","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Using the PRS Model Evaluator framework (read_skill_section: skill_overview), I prioritized (i) endpoint fidelity, (ii) availability of PRS-only performance for fair comparison, (iii) training scale/robustness, and (iv) covariate/packaging clarity. Among candidates, PGS001301 is the only model reporting both PRS-only and full-model metrics with explicit covariates, showing strong PRS-only discrimination (PGS-only AUROC 0.8287; PGS-only R² 0.1422) and a large UKB training set (n=269,704) with EUR evaluation available. Several alternatives report only full-model AUROC (e.g., PGS000040 AUROC 0.90; PGS000316 AUROC 0.879) with covariates listed as unknown, making it unclear how much performance is attributable to the PGS versus covariate packaging; others (PGS001856/PGS002067 etc.) provide only partial-r, which is harder to compare directly to AUROC/R² here. Trait alignment is acceptable: PGS001301 targets “Malabsorption/coeliac disease” mapped to the same EFO (celiac disease), though it is slightly broader than strictly ‘celiac disease’, hence Moderate (not High) confidence.\n\nHeritability sanity-check (get_heritability_records: celiac disease) shows EUR liability-scale h2 estimates in the ~0.15–0.45 range across sources/definitions, consistent with celiac disease having substantial genetic contribution; PGS001301’s PRS-only R² (~0.14) is plausible relative to these ceilings and supports that the reported performance is not obviously implausible."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001174","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity: PGS001174 is a direct match to the target (trait_efo=cholelithiasis) with explicit phenotyping_reported of time-to-event cholelithiasis; other candidates either broaden the endpoint to include cholecystitis (PGS001861/PGS002072) or provide only an OR without standard discrimination/variance metrics (PGS004476/PGS004546/PGS005150). Per the trait-label guidance, phenotyping_reported is the primary endpoint field and composite endpoints are acceptable but not inherently better than a direct endpoint.

Comparable performance evidence: PGS001174 is the only candidate with PRS-only metrics reported (PGS-only AUROC=0.623 and PGS-only R²=0.028 in European validation), plus full-model AUROC and incremental AUROC, giving a clearer view of standalone PGS signal and covariate contribution than partial-r (PGS001861/PGS002072) or single ORs (others). This aligns with the evaluator framework emphasizing comparable PRS-only performance when available.

Trade-offs: PGS001861/PGS002072 have larger training N and report slightly higher partial-r, but lack PRS-only AUROC/R² and are for a broader phenotype (cholelithiasis + cholecystitis). Given the target is cholelithiasis specifically and PGS001174 provides the cleanest direct-endpoint + directly comparable PRS-only performance package, it is preferred."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS002237","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity: PGS002237 directly targets chronic kidney disease stage 3+ with an explicit eGFR threshold (eGFR <45 ml/min/1.73m2), aligning well with the target trait CKD. Several alternatives have weaker/shifted endpoints (e.g., time-to-event chronic renal failure, CKD with dialysis, incident CKD in special subcohorts, or diabetes-subtype-derived labels).

Performance evidence (per performance_metrics guidance): Many candidates report only full-model AUROC/C-index or only effect sizes; PRS-only metrics are largely absent. PGS002237 reports a strong full-model AUROC (~0.78) and a meaningful per-SD effect size (OR 1.47, 95% CI 1.32–1.65), which is supportive of moderate-to-strong PRS signal even though covariates are relatively heavy (so the AUROC is not treated as PRS-only). In contrast, the one candidate with explicit PRS-only metrics (PGS001272) shows weak PRS-only performance (PGS-only AUROC ~0.536; PGS-only R² ~0.002), and the 2023 method-benchmark scores (PGS003988–PGS004158) have modest discrimination (AUROC ~0.55–0.59) despite clean covariates.

Study/design signal: PGS002237 comes from a CKD-focused Nat Med paper explicitly aiming to predict CKD across ancestries, with large development N (n=279,819) and multi-ancestry evaluation, which is a positive robustness/transportability signal relative to smaller framework evaluations.

Heritability sanity check: Local EUR h2 records for chronic kidney disease are low on the observed scale (~0.012–0.019; liability ~0.039–0.057). This supports expecting modest PRS-explained variance overall and cautions against over-interpreting covariate-boosted full-model AUROC; nonetheless, among the direct CKD candidates, PGS002237 has the strongest combined endpoint alignment + effect-size/performance support."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_HIGH_QUALITY","best_model_id":"PGS001783","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"Endpoint fidelity: PGS001783 is a direct match to the target (trait_reported/trait_efo/phenotyping_reported all chronic obstructive pulmonary disease), whereas some alternatives are adjacent or differently packaged (e.g., emphysema; algorithmic-defined; time-to-event; chronic airway obstruction; ICD10 J44-specific).
